title: LucaProt Deep Learning Discovers 161,979 Potential New RNA Virus Species Across Global Ecosystems
whyItMatters: Published in Cell: integrates protein sequence and predicted 3D structure to mine 10,487 global metatranscriptomes, uncovering 161,979 putative RNA virus species and 180 supergroups—the largest single expansion of the RNA virosphere.
summary: Researchers from Sun Yat-sen University, Alibaba Cloud Intelligence (Apsara Lab), and the University of Sydney developed LucaProt, a deep learning model fusing protein sequence embeddings with predicted structural representations to detect highly divergent RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP) sequences invisible to homology-based tools like BLAST. Screening 10,487 global metatranscriptomes spanning hot springs, hydrothermal vents, air, and soil, LucaProt identified 161,979 putative RNA virus species across 180 supergroups—including ultra-long RNA genomes up to 47,250 nucleotides—with a representative subset experimentally confirmed via RT-PCR and RNA/DNA sequencing.
technicalHighlights: Identified 161,979 putative RNA virus species and 180 RNA virus supergroups across 10,487 global metatranscriptomes—dramatically expanding known viral diversity.
Detected deeply divergent RdRP proteins and exceptionally long RNA virus genomes up to 47,250 nucleotides where sequence-only homology fails.
Experimentally confirmed a subset of novel viruses via RT-PCR and RNA/DNA sequencing, with open-source model weights and code (github.com/alibaba/LucaProt).
caveats: The 161,979 figure represents putative viral species defined by RdRP sequence-identity clustering (>90%), with wet-lab RT-PCR confirmation performed on a representative subset rather than all 161,979 species.

scoreRationale.foundational: Executed the largest single expansion of the documented RNA virosphere, uncovering viruses in extreme habitats from hydrothermal vents to the atmosphere.
scoreRationale.ripple: Established sequence-plus-structure deep learning as the standard paradigm for dark-matter viral and microbial discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Cell (2024, PMID 39389057) with direct RT-PCR/sequencing confirmation and open-source code.
scoreRationale.velocity: Uncovered over 160,000 divergent viral species across 10,487 global datasets in a single computational sweep.
